references.text: The original list of materials to be gathered for the tabernacle included blue, purple, and scarlet yarn as well as fine linen.
The use of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn along with finely twisted linen in making the tabernacle curtains.
The curtain for the Most Holy Place was to be made of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen.
The curtain for the tent entrance was to be made from the same materials: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen.
The priestly garments, including the ephod, were to be made of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn as well as fine linen.
The execution of the work on the tabernacle curtains using finely twisted linen and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
The priestly garments were made of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen, as commanded.
Blue cloth and other colored fabrics were used to cover the holy items during transport.
Solomon asked for skilled craftsmen to work with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen for the temple.
The curtain in Solomon's temple was made of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen.
The verses describe respectively the list of materials and the actual act of the people bringing these materials.
